stated: Implement the recommendations of the Infected Blood Inquiry in full, including delivering full and fair compensation to all victims of the scandal in a timely and transparent manner.

source.quote: Implement the recommendations of the Infected Blood Inquiry in full, including delivering full and fair compensation to all victims of the scandal in a timely and transparent manner.

bearing_set.reason: The policy is fundamentally about due process and fair treatment by the state: it responds to a finding that the government and NHS administered contaminated blood products, then suppressed the truth for decades, denying victims legal redress; implementing the inquiry's recommendations — including compensation and accountability — directly concerns victims' rights, due process, and equal treatment under law.

Full compensation payments to victims directly and materially improve real disposable income for a population many of whom have faced severe financial hardship due to illness-related inability to work and decades of inadequate redress.

The compensation scheme alone is projected to cost £10 billion+, representing a material unfunded or newly-funded spending commitment that directly affects the debt path and sustainability of public finances.

membership_note: The policy's primary effects land on justice/due process (O9) and fiscal sustainability (O12). Healthcare safety governance reforms within the inquiry recommendations are real but too narrow to materially shift O3's access/waiting-time indicators; compensation flows to individuals rather than altering prices (O2) or the tax burden (O11).
